newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison 1996 net to rise, core seen weak.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison 1996 net to rise, core seen weak.

text.p: Hutchison Whampoa Ltd has already ensured solid net profit growth in 1996 with a hefty first-half exceptional gain, but recurrent earnings should be weak, analysts said on Friday.
The Hong Kong conglomerate is due to release its calendar 1996 results next Wednesday and analysts forecast net profit of about HK$12 billion compared with HK$9.57 billion in 1995.
Hutchison had interim net profit of HK$7.84 billion, bolstered by a HK$4.1 billion exceptional gain from the listing of its Orange Plc subsidiary in London last April.

"The management was under no pressure to show a good performance in recurring terms because they had a large exceptional in there from a gain on the sale of Orange," said Morgan Stanley analyst Mike Warren.
"They realised an exceptional gain of HK$4 billion, so in absolute terms that really did shore up earnings growth for 1996. They will probably be down in recurring terms," he said.
Warren said he expected net profit of about HK$11.9 billion.
Hutchison is 48.9 percent-owned by Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and has interests in property, energy, telecommunications, container terminal operations and retailing.
"They had some slowdown in the container ports and lower property contributions. The telecom side was quite flat," said Herbert Lau, an analyst at Vickers Ballas.
He forecast net profit of about HK$12 billion.
Analysts said the lack of development profits in 1996 would be the main reason for weak recurrent earnings.
"So-called core earnings will be down because there is less property development earnings," said Carl Wong, associate director at HSBC James Capel.
He also expected net profit of about HK$12 billion.
But Warren said the market had adequately discounted the lack in property development income.
"When one looks forward to 1998, then this company will start to show significant earnings from its property division," he said.

"In container terminals, there was a slowdown in throughput growth at the port but HIT (Hong Kong International Terminals) will have exceeded the throughput growth experienced by the port," added Warren.
Hutchison Port is a major port operator in Hong Kong and owns a number of container ports in the Kwai Chung district through its subsidiary HIT.
Hong Kong's shipping and port services have been hit by a slowdown of cross-border trade with China. However, Warren said Chinese ports would have been a source of stronger growth.
On the telecoms side, analysts said Hutchison had a sharp upturn in subscriber growth. But the costs of increasing the subscriber base were likely to be included in 1996 results.

"I would expect there would be a year-over-year decline in cellular earnings in 1996 against 1995, but a strong rebound in 1997 against 1996," said Warren. "The benefits of increasing their subscribers number on the cellular network will show through in 1997."
Warren has an outperform rating on the stock and a 12-month share price target of HK$73. The stock was up HK$0.25 at HK$55.00 in Friday afternoon trade.

"Where the shares are at the moment, they are a good investment," said Warren. "All round I think most of the core businesses are in good shape going forward, and fundamentally this group looks as good as any of the major conglomerates in Hong Kong."
